data.why: samplespectra.txt ships in the repo and is loaded by app.py as the default Spectra tab text, so the browser agent can also paste it in to test alternate spectra.

goals: Enter a peptide sequence (with optional modifications) and a charge range to generate the full set of theoretical fragment ions
Toggle fragment ion types (a/b/c/x/y/z) and monoisotopic vs average mass to see how the fragment table and segment plot change
Paste or edit an experimental spectrum (m/z intensity pairs) and match it against the calculated fragments within a chosen tolerance
Inspect which fragment ions were matched in the annotated spectra bar chart and the highlighted sequence coverage table
Read off Hyperscore and Binomial Score summarizing the quality of the spectrum match
Download the fragment ion table and the matched spectra results as CSV for downstream analysis

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree of fragment calculation and spectrum annotation. All ten screens I opened match their nodes, labels are clean at both levels, and the features are mostly well cut. It needs small fixes before filing: add URL-parameter presets and candidate comparison, cover internal-fragment matching, and surface the coverage-table y-ion bug on the node it affects.
